issues.legal_issue: A conveyance of a proprietary share that includes associated agricultural lands, while expressly excluding only a different category of land, transfers the disputed land if it is within the conveyed share and not within the exclusion.
material_facts: The purchasers acquired an eight-annas proprietary share together with the associated lands and interests.
The sale deed described the conveyed property broadly and excluded only chaukidari chakran land.
The disputed land was part of the conveyed proprietary share and was not within the stated exclusion.
issues.conclusion: The sale deed included the disputed land, so the purchasers acquired it.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the sale deed according to its broad description of the property conveyed and its specific exclusion of only chaukidari chakran land; no statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: possession_recovery_suit and purchase_of_proprietary_share and deed_covers_associated_lands and disputed_land_not_excluded

predicates.possession_recovery_suit: A claimant brought a suit to recover possession of land.
predicates.purchase_of_proprietary_share: The claimant purchased a proprietary share associated with the disputed land.
predicates.deed_covers_associated_lands: The conveyance describes the proprietary share as including its associated lands and interests.
predicates.disputed_land_not_excluded: The disputed land is not within a category expressly excluded from the conveyance.

issues.definition: When a possession-recovery suit concerns land associated with a purchased proprietary share, and the conveyance covers that land without excluding it, the purchaser acquired the disputed land.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee who entered possession only under the mortgage has no right to retain possession after the mortgage is redeemed.
material_facts: The defendants entered possession of the disputed land under mortgage deeds and had no prior connection with it.
The plaintiffs redeemed the mortgages in 1943.
The courts below rejected the defendants’ claim that they held an independent raiyati interest in the land.
issues.conclusion: After redemption, the defendants had no right to remain in possession under the mortgages.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the ordinary consequence of redemption: possession held only as mortgagees no longer entitled the mortgagees to retain the land once the mortgage was redeemed. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: possession_recovery_suit and possession_began_under_mortgage and mortgage_redeemed and no_independent_land_right

predicates.possession_recovery_suit: A claimant brought a suit to recover possession of land.
predicates.possession_began_under_mortgage: The occupants entered possession of the land only by virtue of a mortgage.
predicates.mortgage_redeemed: The mortgage was redeemed before the claim to recover possession was decided.
predicates.no_independent_land_right: The occupants did not establish an independent right to the land.

issues.definition: If occupants entered land only under a mortgage, the mortgage was redeemed, and they have no independent land right, they have no right to retain possession in a possession-recovery suit.

issues.legal_issue: Long possession by occupants whose possession began only as mortgagees does not estop the owner from seeking recovery of possession.
material_facts: The defendants’ possession began under the mortgage deeds.
The defendants had no prior connection with the land, and their claimed independent raiyati interest was rejected.
The plaintiffs sought possession after redeeming the mortgages.
issues.conclusion: The defendants’ long possession did not estop the plaintiffs from recovering possession.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that long possession did not estop the claimants in the circumstances because the defendants possessed the land only as mortgagees; no statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: possession_recovery_suit and possession_began_under_mortgage and no_independent_land_right and long_possession

predicates.possession_recovery_suit: A claimant brought a suit to recover possession of land.
predicates.possession_began_under_mortgage: The occupants entered possession of the land only by virtue of a mortgage.
predicates.no_independent_land_right: The occupants did not establish an independent right to the land.
predicates.long_possession: The occupants remained in possession for a lengthy period.

issues.definition: In a possession-recovery suit, long possession does not estop the claimant when the occupants entered only as mortgagees and have no independent land right.

issues.legal_issue: A possession-recovery suit filed within twelve years after redemption of the mortgage is not barred by limitation on the ground that the claimant was not in possession during that period.
material_facts: The suit was instituted within twelve years of redemption.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the twelve-year limitation period to the claim and held that the period was satisfied because the suit was brought within twelve years of redemption; no earlier case was relied on for this issue.

predicates.possession_recovery_suit: A claimant brought a suit to recover possession of land.
predicates.claim_follows_mortgage_redemption: The claim to recover possession followed redemption of a mortgage under which the occupants had possessed the land.
predicates.suit_filed_within_applicable_limitation_: The claimant filed the suit within the applicable limitation period measured from the relevant event.

issues.definition: A possession-recovery claim following mortgage redemption is not barred by limitation when the suit is filed within the applicable limitation period.

issues.legal_issue: When an estate vests in the State, a former proprietor cannot recover land from its occupants unless the land is within an interest saved from vesting, and a subsisting title to possession alone does not make land the proprietor’s khas possession.
material_facts: The estate vested in the State while the appeal was pending.
The mortgages had been redeemed in 1943, so no mortgage subsisted on the vesting date.
On the vesting date, the respondents were not in possession by cultivating the land themselves, through servants or hired labour, or with hired stock.
The land did not fall within any applicable category of land saved under section 6 of the Bihar Land Reforms Act.
The respondents’ claim rested on their asserted right to recover possession, rather than on actual khas possession at vesting.
issues.conclusion: The respondents’ interests, including the right to recover possession, vested in the State; they could not recover possession from the appellants after vesting.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3(1) and 4(a) and (f) of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950, the estate and the proprietor’s interests vested in the State, except interests expressly saved by the Act, and the Collector took charge of the vested interests. Section 2(k) defined khas possession by reference to actual possession through specified forms of cultivation or horticultural operations. Section 6(1), including clause (c) as substituted by the Bihar Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1959, saved qualifying lands, including land forming the subject of a subsisting mortgage on redemption of which the intermediary was entitled to recover khas possession. Because no mortgage subsisted at vesting and the land was not in khas possession or otherwise saved, section 6 did not preserve the respondents’ interest. The Court followed the approach to vesting in Haji Sk. Subhan v. Madhorao, [1962] Supp. 1 S.C.R. 123, and rejected the broader reading of khas possession in Brijnandan Singh v. Jamuna Prasad, A.I.R. 1958 Pat. 589.

rule.if: possession_recovery_suit and estate_vested_in_state and not land_in_khas_possession_at_vesting and not subsisting_qualifying_mortgage and not land_in_other_saved_category

predicates.possession_recovery_suit: A former proprietor brought a suit to recover possession of land from its occupants.
predicates.estate_vested_in_state: The estate containing the land vested in the State.
predicates.land_in_khas_possession_at_vesting: At vesting, the proprietor possessed the land through cultivation or horticultural operations by the proprietor, servants, hired labour, or hired stock.
predicates.subsisting_qualifying_mortgage: At vesting, a mortgage subsisted over the land and its redemption would entitle the intermediary to recover khas possession.
predicates.land_in_other_saved_category: The land fell within another category of land expressly saved from vesting.

issues.definition: If an estate vested in the State and the land was neither in the proprietor’s khas possession nor covered by a qualifying subsisting mortgage or another saved category, the former proprietor cannot recover possession in a possession-recovery suit.
